paragraphs: Reduce a PDF's file size before sharing it or storing it. Compression results depend on the images, fonts and other content already in the document.
steps: Add the PDF you want to compress.
Choose the compression settings available in the workspace and run Compress.
Compare the output size and readability with the original, then save the result.
compress.limitations: A PDF that is already optimized may not become smaller. Stronger compression can reduce image quality; check small text and diagrams before sharing the output.

paragraphs: Combine multiple PDF documents into one file. The order you choose determines the order of the documents in the merged result.
steps: Add the PDF files you want to combine.
Arrange the files in the desired order and review the available settings.
Run Merge, check the page sequence and save the combined PDF.
merge.limitations: Check bookmarks, page numbering and forms in the merged output. Keep the original documents, particularly when working with digitally signed files.

paragraphs: Divide a PDF into smaller documents using the splitting options shown in the workspace. This is useful when only part of a document needs to be shared.
steps: Add the PDF you want to split.
Choose the split method and page ranges or other options offered by the tool.
Run Split and review each output document before saving it.
split.limitations: Check page ranges against the document's actual page positions, which may differ from printed page numbers.

paragraphs: Remove selected sensitive content from a PDF using redaction. Redaction is different from placing a visible shape over content that may still be extractable.
steps: Open the PDF and choose the content to redact.
Review your selections and apply redaction using the tool's controls.
Save a separate result and check that the intended information cannot be read, searched or copied.
redact.limitations: Review the entire output, including other pages and document metadata. Selecting a redaction area alone does not finish the operation; apply the redactions and verify the saved file.

paragraphs: Use optical character recognition to recognize text in scanned PDF pages. Recognition depends on scan quality, language selection and page orientation.
steps: Add the scanned PDF.
Choose the language and OCR settings available on your deployment.
Run OCR and check the recognized text against the scan.
ocr.limitations: OCR can misread handwriting, low-resolution scans and complex layouts. Verify names, numbers and other important text manually. Available languages depend on the deployment.

paragraphs: Open a PDF to read its pages and use the viewing or annotation controls available in the workspace.
steps: Open the PDF you want to read.
Navigate the document and use the available zoom, search and annotation controls.
If you make changes, save the result and check it before sharing.
read.limitations: Scanned pages may need OCR before their text can be searched. Password-protected files may require the document password.

paragraphs: Convert documents using the input and output formats offered by the conversion tool. Review the selected format before starting.
steps: Choose the conversion direction and add a supported file.
Review the output format and available settings.
Run the conversion and check the layout and content of the result.
convert.limitations: Conversion can change fonts, tables and page layout. Available formats depend on your deployment and its installed processing tools. Scanned PDFs may need OCR for editable text.

paragraphs: Open a PDF in the workspace to choose editing, annotation and document-processing tools. Keep an original copy so you can compare your changes.
steps: Open your document in the PDF workspace.
Choose a tool and apply the changes you need.
Review the document and save the result.
/editor.limitations: Individual tools have different format and processing requirements. Modifying a digitally signed document can affect its signature validity.
